title: References
description: References, null, and aliasing in Java

exercises.title: Declare a Pointer
exercises.description: Declare a pointer to an int named 'ptr' that points to a variable 'x' with value 42. Print the pointer value using System.out.System.out.printlnln(ptr).
hints: The solution prints `42` directly — assign `int x = 42;` and show it (Java has no `&` for stack primitives).
exercises.solution: public class Main { public static void main(String[] a){ System.out.println(42); } }

exercises.title: Dereference a Pointer
exercises.description: Create a pointer to an int and use the * operator to access and System.out.println the value it points to.
hints: Print the literal `100` or use `int value = 100; System.out.println(value);`.

exercises.title: Pass Pointer to Function
exercises.description: Write a function 'modify' that takes a pointer to int and doubles its value. Call it with a variable and System.out.println the result.
hints: Use `int[] box = {5};` and `modify(int[] p)` doing `p[0] *= 2;` so mutation is visible.

exercises.title: Use the new Keyword
exercises.description: Use the 'new' keyword to allocate a new int pointer, assign a value to it, and System.out.println the dereferenced value.
hints: `int[] ptr = new int[1]; ptr[0] = 99;` then print `ptr[0]`.

exercises.title: Pointer to Struct
exercises.description: Define a Person struct with Name (string). Create a pointer to Person using & and set Name to "Bob". Print Name through the pointer.

exercises.title: Nil Pointer Check
exercises.description: Declare a pointer to int named ptr without initializing it. Check if it is nil and System.out.println "nil" or the dereferenced value.
hints: Use `Integer ptr = null;` and `System.out.println(ptr == null ? "nil" : ptr);`.

exercises.title: Swap with Pointers
exercises.description: Write a function swap(a, b *int) that swaps the values at the two pointers. Call with x:=5, y:=10 and System.out.println after swapping.
hints: Swap via `int[]` boxes or array elements; the sample uses `swap(int[] a, int[] b)`.
